Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:10:1.english: Even for a borrower, [the court] appraises - And [this] refers to "for damages" [mentioned earlier].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:10:2.english: Or perhaps [the court] does not appraise even for a borrower - And this "even" refers to a thief and a robber.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:12:1.hebrew: מדאמרי ליה רב כהנא ורב אסי - בבבא מציעא בפ' השואל (דף צו:):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:12:1.english: From [the fact] that Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to him - [This is] in Bava Metzia, in the chapter [entitled] HaSho'el (96b).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:14:1.hebrew: שליא שיצתה כו' - דקי"ל המפלת שליא, יושבת עליה ימי טומאה וימי טהרה, שאין שליא בלא ולד, אלא שנימוח בתוכה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:14:1.english: An afterbirth that emerged, etc. - For we hold [that] a woman who miscarries an afterbirth observes for it days of ritual impurity and days of ritual purity, for there is no afterbirth without a fetus; rather, [it is] that [the fetus] dissolved within it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:14:2.hebrew: מונין לה מן הראשון - דמיום ראשון טמאה, ואפי' הואי לידה יבישתה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:14:2.english: One counts for her from the first [day] - For from the first day she is ritually impure, and even if it was a dry birth [without blood].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:15:1.english: To act stringently - That we render impure ritually pure items that she touched on the first [day] from the time of the emergence of the amniotic sac.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:16:1.hebrew: דקא מטהרת לה מראשון - שתהא סופרת י"ד של נקבה עם יום הראשון, ודמים שתראה ביום ט"ו טהורין, דהיינו קולא, דאי הויא מניא משני, לא חיילא ימי טהרה עד למחר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:16:1.english: You will render her pure from the first [day] - That she will count fourteen [days] of a female [birth] with the first day, and blood that she sees on the fifteenth day [will be] pure — which is a leniency, for if she were to count from the second [day], the days of purity would not take effect until the next day.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:17:1.english: She should be concerned - to render impure ritually pure items that she touches on the first [day].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:17:2.english: Counting, she does not count - the two weeks of a female [birth] except from the second [day].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:18:1.hebrew: מאי קמ"ל - עולא דאמר חוששת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:18:1.english: What is he teaching us - Ulla, who said [that] she is concerned.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:18:2.hebrew: דאין מקצת שליא בלא ולד - ומש"ה חוששת שמא רוב מיחוי הולד יצא באותו מקצת, ומכי נפק רוב, הוי ליה כילוד, כדאמרינן במסכת נדה (דף כח.): "יצא מחותך או מסורס, עד שיצא רובו". ומימנא ודאי לא מניא מראשון, דשמא לא נפק רובא עד שני. דאי יש מקצת שליא בלא ולד, לא הוה חיישינן לטמא טהרות, דכולי האי לא חיישינן דנימא תרי חומרי — דלמא נפקא ורוב נפקא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:18:2.english: That part of an afterbirth [cannot emerge] without a fetus - And therefore [the woman] must be concerned that perhaps the majority of the dissolved fetus emerged in that part [of the afterbirth]; and once the majority has emerged, it is considered as born, as we say in Tractate Niddah (28a): "[If a fetus] emerged limb by limb or feet first, [it is not considered born] until its majority emerges." And [regarding] counting [her days], she certainly does not count from the first [day], because perhaps the majority did not emerge until the second [day]. For if there could be part of an afterbirth without a fetus, we would not be concerned to render pure foods impure [on the first day], because we are not concerned to such an extent as to apply two stringencies: perhaps [a fetus] emerged [with it], and [moreover] the majority [of it] emerged.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:18:4.english: [An afterbirth] part of which emerged - Prior to the slaughter of the animal.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:18:5.hebrew: אסורה - כולה, ואע"פ שאין בה ולד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:18:5.english: [It is] prohibited - All of it, even though there is no fetus in it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:18:6.hebrew: ה"ג סימן ולד באשה וסימן ולד בבהמה - כלומר, מפני שהשליא סימן ולד בין באשה בין בבהמה, שאין שליא בלא ולד אלא שנימוח, וחיישינן שמא באותו מקצת שיצא קודם שחיטה היה רובו של עובר. וקיימא לן: יצא רובו, ה"ז כילוד, ואינו ניתר בשחיטת האם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:18:6.english: This is how we read [the text]: A sign of a fetus in a woman and a sign of a fetus in an animal - That is to say, because the afterbirth is a sign of a fetus both in a woman and in an animal — since there is no afterbirth without a fetus, rather [the fetus] dissolved — we are concerned lest in that part that emerged prior to slaughter was the majority of the fetus. And we hold [as established law]: [if] its majority emerged, behold, it is like one born and is not permitted by the slaughter of the mother.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:1:1.hebrew: ופטור - דשומר שכר פטור באונסין, כדכתיב ביה: "ומת או נשבר או נשבה אין רואה, שבועת ה' תהיה בין שניהם" (שמות כ״ב:ט׳-י׳):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:1:1.english: And [he is] exempt - For a paid bailee is exempt in [cases of] unavoidable accident, as it is written regarding him: "And [if] it dies, or is broken, or is driven away, no one seeing [it], an oath of the Lord shall be between them both" (Exodus 22:9-10).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:1:3.hebrew: לב"ד - לשומה כמה היא שוה, והכי משמע קרא: "יביאהו עד" — יביא העדודה, כדכתיב (בראשית מ״ט:כ״ז) "בבקר יאכל עד", דהיינו שלל, כדמתרגמינן "עדאה". מפי מורי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:1:3.english: To court - To appraise it [to see] how much it is worth. And this is what the verse means: "He shall bring it [as] ed" — he shall bring the carcass [adudah], as it is written (Genesis 49:27), "In the morning he shall devour the prey [ad]," which means "spoil," as we translate [it into Aramaic as] adah. [This explanation is] from the mouth of my teacher.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:2:1.hebrew: מאי לאו בהא קמיפלגי - דבאונסין, הא ודאי לא פליג אבא שאול למימר דאפי' נטרפה באונס יהא חייב, דאין שומר שכר חייב באונסין. אלא ה"ק: אם נטרפה בפשיעה, שיהא בר תשלומין, יביא עדודה ויוסיף מביתו על הדמים שהיא שוה בשעת מיתה. דאי משום דמים דהשתא, לא איצטריך; דהשתא אי אית ליה נבילות אחרנייתא יהיב ליה, כל שכן הא! אלא לפחת נבילה אתא. ות"ק, דלא מפיק ליה להך דרשה, סבר פחת נבילה דמזיק הוי. הלכך, לא מצי לאוקמי לקרא להך דרשה, דאי משום דמים דהשתא, לא איצטריך, דהא תניא: "ישיב" – לרבות שוה כסף:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:2:1.english: What, is it not that they disagree about this - For regarding unavoidable accidents, Abba Shaul certainly does not disagree to say that even if it was torn by an unavoidable accident he would be liable, since a paid bailee is not liable for unavoidable accidents. Rather, this is what he is saying: if it was torn through negligence, such that he is subject to payment, he brings its carcass and adds from his own [funds] onto the value that it was worth at the time of death. For if [the verse] were [teaching] regarding its current value, it would not be needed, since now, if he has other carcasses he may give them to him [as payment] — all the more so this [carcass itself]! Rather, [the verse] comes [to teach] regarding the depreciation of the carcass. And the Tanna Kamma, who does not derive this exposition from it, holds [that] the depreciation of the carcass belongs to the damager. Therefore, he cannot establish the verse for this exposition, since if it were [teaching] regarding its current value, it is not needed, for it was taught [in a baraita]: "He shall return" — [this comes] to include anything of monetary value.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:3:1.hebrew: בטורח נבילה - להביאה ממקום שמתה שם למקום שהיתה שם, אבא שאול סבר על המזיק הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:3:1.english: Concerning the effort of [retrieving] the carcass - To bring it from the place where it died to the place where it was; Abba Shaul holds [that it] is upon the damager.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:4:1.english: And it is taught - [Said] calmly [i.e., as a statement, not as a question].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:4:2.english: He shall restore money to its owner, and the dead [animal] - [This] implies that he shall also restore the dead [animal] to its owner.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:6:1.hebrew: בדנפשיה קא טרח - וריוח דנפשיה קא עביד, דשיים ליה לניזק בדמי יתירי, ולמה לי קרא דוהמת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:6:1.english: He is expending effort for his own [sake] - And he is making a profit for himself, for he appraises it for the injured party at a higher value; so why do I need the verse [that states] "and the dead [animal]"?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:6:2.english: And at the edge - [At] the edge of the pit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:8:2.hebrew: בדברא - בשדה, ואע"ג שמחוסר הבאה לעיר, נמכר בזוז:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:8:2.english: In the field - [This means] in the field; and even though it still needs to be brought to the city, [the beam] is sold for a zuz.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:9:1.hebrew: אמר שמואל - מנהג דיינין הוא שאין שמין לא לגנב ולא לגזלן, שאם גנב וגזל בהמה או כלים ונפחתו אצלו, אין שמין הנבילה והשברים לבעלים שיחזיר גנב הפחת, אלא ישלם בהמה וכלים מעולים, והשברים שלו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:9:1.english: Shmuel says - It is the practice of the judges that they do not appraise for either a thief or a robber: if one stole or robbed an animal or vessels and they depreciated in his possession, they do not appraise the carcass or the broken pieces for the owner so that the thief would [merely] return the depreciation; rather, he must pay [for] a prime [undamaged] animal and vessels, and the broken pieces [remain] his.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:9:2.hebrew: אלא לנזקין - שמין, כדכתיב והמת יהיה לו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:9:2.english: Rather, for damages - [They] appraise [the carcass], as it is written: "And the dead [animal] shall be his."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11a:9:3.english: And I say: even for a borrower, and Abba concedes to me - [i.e.,] Rav.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:16:1.hebrew: דקא מטהרת לה מראשון - פירוש: שסופרת י"ד של נקבה מראשון, והדמים שתראה בט"ו יהיו טהורין. וא"ת: ואמאי לא יהיו טהורים? דלמא ביום ראשון יצא ראשו או רובו, ואפי' לא יצא, דלמא הוא זכר. וי"ל: דלא מצי למישרי מספק ספיקא, דהוו תרי קולי דסתרי אהדדי; שאם תראה יום מ"א תשתרי נמי מספק ספיקא, דשמא לא יצא רובו ביום ראשון, ואפי' יצא רוב — דלמא נקבה היא. והשתא, בתחילה התרנו משום דשמא זכר, השתא נתירנו משום שמא נקבה — הרי ממה נפשך נעשה איסור. וכה"ג תנן בהמפלת (נדה כט.): תשב לזכר ולנקבה ולנדה, אע"ג דכל איסור באפי נפשיה הוי ספק ספיקא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:16:1.english: "Because you declare her pure from the first [day]" - Explanation: [the concern is] that she counts the fourteen [impure days] of a female [birth] from the first [day], and the blood that she sees on the fifteenth [day] will be [considered] pure. And if you ask: Why should it not be pure? Perhaps on the first day its head or its majority emerged, and even if it did not emerge, perhaps it is a male. And one can answer that we cannot permit [it] based on a double doubt, because these are two leniencies that contradict each other. For if she sees [blood] on the forty-first day, she would also be permitted based on a double doubt: perhaps its majority did not emerge on the first day, and even if the majority did emerge, perhaps it is a female. Now, at first we permitted [her] because perhaps [it is] a male, and now we permit [her] because perhaps [it is] a female — thus, either way, a prohibition is violated. And similarly we learned in [the chapter] Hamapelet (Niddah 29a): "She must sit [in impurity] for a male, and for a female, and for a niddah," even though each prohibition on its own is a double doubt.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:18:1.hebrew: דאין מקצת שליא בלא ולד - וא"ת: לר"א, דאמר חוששין משום דאין מקצת שליא בלא ולד, אבל אם היה מקצת שליא בלא ולד לא היתה חוששת — ה"ד? אי ברה"ר, אפי' בחד ספיקא מטהרי'; ואי ברה"י, אפי' בספק ספיקא נמי טמא, דהא תנן (טהרות פ"ו מ"ד): "כל ספיקות שאתה יכול להרבות ברה"י — אפי' ספק ספיקא טמא". וי"ל: דשמעתין איירי לענין לאוסרה לבעלה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:18:1.english: "That there is no part of an afterbirth without a fetus" - And if you ask: According to Rabbi Elazar, who says we are concerned [that she gave birth on the first day] because there is no part of an afterbirth without a fetus, [implying that] if part of an afterbirth were [able to emerge] without a fetus, she would not be concerned — what are the circumstances? If [it occurred] in a public domain, even in [a case of] a single doubt we declare [her] pure; and if [it occurred] in a private domain, even in [a case of] a double doubt [she is] also impure, for we learned [in a Mishnah] (Tahorot 6:4): "All doubts that you can multiply in a private domain — even a double doubt is impure." And one can answer: Our sugya is dealing with [the matter of] forbidding her to her husband.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:18:2.hebrew: שליא שיצתה מקצתה אסורה באכילה - פי': אסורה אפי' מה שבפנים, דשמא באותו מקצת שיצא, יצא ראשו של ולד והוי כולו כילוד, ולא קרינן ביה "כל בבהמה תאכלו"; דאם יש מקצת שליא בלא ולד, היה לנו להתיר מטעם ס"ס. תימה, דסוגיא דהכא מוכח דשרי ר' אלעזר בשליא שיצתה מקצתה אי הוי ס"ס באכילה, ובסוף בהמה המקשה (חולין עז:) משמע דאפילו בס"ס אסר רבי אלעזר — דעל הך משנה ד"שליא שיצתה מקצתה" קאמר ר' אלעזר: לא שנו אלא בשאינו קשורה בולד, אבל קשורה בולד אין חוששין לולד אחר; ובשאין קשורה, ע"כ לא הוי אלא ס"ס, כדקתני בברייתא דקתני התם: "שמא נימוח שפיר של שליא כו'". וא"כ, כשאין קשורה תשתרי, דשמא אין שם ולד אחר, ואפי' יש שם ולד אחר שמא לא יצא רובו! וי"ל: ברייתא דקתני התם "שמא כו'" מיירי בשליא של אחר הולד, ור' אלעזר איירי בשליא שקודם הולד, דודאי יש שם ולד אחר כשאין קשורה בה, כדאמרינן בהמפלת (נדה דף כו:) דלא אמרינן "תולין את השליא בולד" אלא בשליא הבאה אחר הולד. ועוד י"ל, דהתם אסרי בס"ס גזירה מקצת אטו כולה, כדאמרינן בשמעתין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:18:2.english: An afterbirth that partially emerged is prohibited for eating - Explanation: Even that which is inside [the mother] is prohibited, for perhaps within that part that emerged, the head of a fetus emerged, and the entire [fetus] is considered as born, and we do not apply to it [the verse], "Everything among the animals you may eat." For if there [could be] part of an afterbirth without a fetus, we would have to permit [it] on account of a double doubt (sefek sefeika). [This is] surprising, for the sugya here proves that R' Elazar would permit [eating] an afterbirth that partially emerged if it were a double doubt, yet at the end of [chapter] Behemah HaMaksheh (Chullin 77b) it is implied that R' Elazar prohibits [it] even in [a case of] a double doubt! For regarding this Mishnah of "An afterbirth that partially emerged," R' Elazar says: They only taught [this] when it is not attached to a fetus, but when it is attached to a fetus, we are not concerned for another fetus. And when it is not attached [to a fetus], perforce it is only a double doubt, as the Baraita taught there: "Perhaps the sac of the afterbirth dissolved, etc." And if so, when it is not attached it should be permitted! For perhaps there is no other fetus there, and even if there is another fetus there, perhaps its majority did not emerge! And one can answer: The Baraita that teaches there "Perhaps, etc." is dealing with an afterbirth [that comes] after the fetus, whereas R' Elazar is dealing with an afterbirth [that comes] before the fetus, where there is certainly another fetus there when it is not attached to it, as we say in [chapter] HaMappelet (Niddah 26b), that we do not say "we attribute the afterbirth to the fetus" except in [the case of] an afterbirth that comes after the fetus. And furthermore, one can answer that there they prohibit [it even] in a double doubt [as] a decree [concerning] part [of the afterbirth] on account of the entire [afterbirth], as we say in our sugya.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:18:3.hebrew: כסימן ולד באשה [כך] סימן ולד בבהמה - וא"ת: ואמאי תולה בהמה באשה, ומתני' לא מיירי אלא בבהמה? ויש לומר: משום דבאשה פשוט לו יותר מבבהמה, דהרי שפיר שהוא סימן ולד באשה ולא בבהמה, כדתנן בהלוקח (בכורות דף יט:): סימן ולד בבהמה — שליא, ובאשה — שפיר ושליא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:18:3.english: Just as [it is] a sign of a fetus in a woman, [so too is it] a sign of a fetus in an animal - And if you ask: Why does [the Mishnah] make [the law of] an animal dependent on [that of] a woman, when the Mishnah speaks only of an animal? One can say: Because in a woman it is more obvious to [the Tanna] than in an animal; for behold, [there is] the amniotic sac, which is a sign of a fetus in a woman and not in an animal, as we learned in [the chapter] HaLoke'aḥ (Bekhorot 19b): The sign of a fetus in an animal is an afterbirth, and in a woman, an amniotic sac and an afterbirth.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:1:1.hebrew: יביא עדים שנטרפה באונס - ואיסי דורש בפרק האומנין (ב"מ פג.): "אין רואה" — הא יש רואה, יביא עדים שנטרפה ופטור; דמשמעות דורשין איכא בינייהו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:1:1.english: He should bring witnesses that it was mauled through circumstances beyond his control - And Isi expounds in the chapter [entitled] HaOmanin (Bava Metzia 83a): "[If] there is no one who sees" — [implying that] if there is someone who sees, he must bring witnesses that it was mauled and he is exempt; for [the difference] between them is [merely] the implication [they] expound [from the verses].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:1:2.hebrew: יביא ארורה לב"ד - פי' שמתה בלא ברכה. ואית דגרס "עדורה", כמו "אחת מהנה לא נעדרה" (ישעיהו ל״ד:ט״ז). ובקונטרס גריס "עדודה", כמו "יאכל עד":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:1:2.english: "He shall bring [the] cursed one [arurah] to court" - [This] means that it died without a blessing. And there are those who read adurah, like [the verse], "Not one of them shall be missing" (Isaiah 34:16). And in the Kuntres [Rashi], he reads adudah, like [the verse], "he devours prey [ad]" [Genesis 49:27].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:9:1.hebrew: בשאלתות דרב אחאי <abbr title="גריס">גרי'</abbr>: "אמר שמואל: אמר לי אבא", ולא <abbr title="כפירוש הקונטרס">כפ"ה</abbr> דפירש דמנהג דיינין כך הוא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:9:1.english: In the She'iltot of Rav Achai, it reads: "Shmuel said: Abba said to me," and not like the commentary of the Kuntres [Rashi], who explained that such is the practice of judges.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:9:2.hebrew: אין שמין לא לגנב ולא לגזלן - פ"ה: אין שמין הנבילה והשברים לבעלים שיחזיר הגנב הפחת, אלא ישלם בהמה שלימה וכלים מעולים, והשברים שלו. ואע"ג דקיימא לן "ישיב" — לרבות שוה כסף ככסף, ואפי' סובין, גנב וגזלן שאני, משום דכתיב "אשר גזל" — כעין שגזל; הלכך צריך להחזיר הגזילה או דמיה, ולא סובין. וכן משמע בירושלמי: מנין שאין שמין לא לגנב ולא לגזלן? א"ר אבא בר ממל: "חיים שנים ישלם" — ולא מתים. עד כדון גניבה; גזילה מנין? א"ר אבא בר ממל: "והשיב הגזלה אשר גזל" — כאשר גזל. והיינו טעמא: דגנב וגזלן קנו מיד כשהוציאו מרשות בעלים, אבל מזיק לא נתחייב אלא כמו שהזיק. וה"ט דמ"ד "אף לשואל": כיון דחייב באונסין, נמצא שקנאו משעה שהוציא מיד הבעלים, והדמים הוא דנתחייב כמו גנב וגזלן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11a:9:2.english: They do not appraise either for a thief or for a robber - Rashi explains: We do not appraise the carcass or the broken pieces for the owner so that the thief returns [only] the depreciation; rather, he must pay [for] a whole animal or undamaged vessels, and the broken pieces are his. And even though we hold [as established law that the verse] "he shall return" [comes] to include anything of monetary value as equivalent to money, and even bran, a thief and a robber are different, because it is written, "[the robbed item] that he robbed" — [meaning] in the manner that he robbed [it]; therefore, he must return the robbed item or its monetary value, and not bran. And so it is implied in the Yerushalmi: From where [do we derive] that we do not appraise either for a thief or for a robber? Rabbi Abba bar Mamal said: "Alive... he shall pay double" — and not dead [animals]. So far [we have derived this for] theft; from where [do we derive it for] robbery? Rabbi Abba bar Mamal said: "He shall return the robbed item that he robbed" — [meaning] just as he robbed [it]. And this is the reason: for a thief and a robber acquire [the item] immediately when they remove [it] from the owner's possession, whereas a damager is obligated only according to what he damaged. And this is [also] the reason of the one who says "even for a borrower": since he is liable for unavoidable accidents, it follows that he acquired it from the moment he removed [it] from the owner's hand, and it is [for] the monetary value that he became obligated, just like a thief and a robber.
